title: Training Notes: Maintenance Continuity on a Harbison Parts-and-Labor Protection Transfer
content:
**What is the maintenance-continuity share?**
On a home-sale transfer of a Harbison 10-Year Parts & Labor Protection, Harbison 12-Year Total Protection or Harbison 12-Year Total Protection Plus contract of Harbison Protection Contracts, the maintenance-continuity share applies by multiplication to the open benefit carried to the buyer.

**Which maintenance counts?**
The latest documented maintenance on a covered unit recorded by the date of handling, being the latest of: the completed Comfort Club tune-ups recorded on the primary covered unit and on the paired covered unit (read from Comfort Club Maintenance Agreements visit records), and the latest precision tune-up charge line on the holder's Harbison invoices.

**How is it measured, and what share follows?**
In whole calendar months from that latest record to the closing date on the transfer request:

| Whole calendar months from the latest documented maintenance to the closing date | Maintenance-continuity share |
|---|---|
| 12 months or more | 0.75 |
| 7 to 11 months | 0.90 |
| 6 months or fewer, a record dated after the closing included | 1 |

Where no documented maintenance is recorded on a covered unit at all, there is no recent record to measure from, and the 12-months-or-more share of 0.75 applies.

**Where are the lines?** 6 months: 1. 7 months: 0.90. 11 months: 0.90. 12 months: 0.75.

**Examples (hypothetical; closing date 1 June 2026).**

- Latest record a cooling-season tune-up on the outdoor unit completed 15 April 2025: 13 whole months — share 0.75.
- Latest record a precision tune-up charge line posted 20 October 2025: 7 whole months — share 0.90.
- Latest record a heating-season tune-up on the paired furnace completed 10 June 2026, after the closing but before the date of handling: share 1.
